title: Order spike: splitting governor headroom across four resources
prompt: A flash sale multiplies order inserts. The order trigger parses a JSON payload and runs pricing validation for each record, loads account and price-book data with one relationship query per batch, and hands fulfillment to subscribers through Platform Events. How should the architect split the 100-point capacity budget across the four resources?
detail: Each point reserves a share of per-transaction governor headroom for the spike. A resource that runs out of headroom throws a limit exception and rolls back the whole order batch.

categories.label: SOQL queries and row locks
categories.description: Headroom for SOQL queries per transaction and FOR UPDATE locks on parent records.

categories.label: Apex CPU time
categories.description: Headroom for trigger logic, JSON parsing, and pricing validation in each transaction.

categories.label: Heap and Platform Cache
categories.description: Headroom for in-memory collections and the Platform Cache partition that holds reference data.

categories.label: Platform Event publishing
categories.description: Headroom for publishing the fulfillment events that hand work to asynchronous subscribers.

analysis: JSON parsing and pricing validation run once per order, so Apex CPU time (10,000 ms per synchronous transaction) grows with every record in the batch and is the limit the spike reaches first; it needs the extra headroom. One relationship query per batch keeps the SOQL count flat as volume grows, and Platform Event subscribers run fulfillment in their own asynchronous transactions, so neither needs more than its baseline. Extra heap or cache shortens none of the per-record validation, so it buys no margin against the CPU limit.
